title: Prospective comparison of conservative, outpatient surgical, and inpatient surgical therapy for acute traumatic lesions to the prepatellar and olceranon bursa
summary:
Bursae are small fluid-filled cushions that function as shock absorbers and sliding pads, reducing friction between bones and soft tissues.
The superficially located bursae at the elbow and knee are frequently injured in the course of falls. Once a bursa is opened by an injury, germs can enter it and cause an infection that is sometimes difficult to control. Therefore, in many parts of the world, it is still common practice to remove a bursa opened by an injury in surgery, which means a stay in a hospital and usually general anesthesia for the patient. However, there are no large, high-quality studies to support this common practice. Thus, whether surgery, hospitalization, and anesthesia are really necessary to prevent infection of the opened bursa is still questionable. 
The present study aims to investigate whether less invasive treatment of injury-related bursal openings without surgery, inpatient stay, and general anesthesia can achieve similarly results while providing several benefits to the patient and the health care system:
 1. Avoidance of hospital-related risks (infection with hospital germs, pneumonia due to bed confinement, psychological traumatization due to unfamiliar surroundings up to delirium).
2. Avoidance of surgery-related risks (cardiovascular arrest, death, injury to the pharyngeal mucosa, positioning damage during surgery)
3. Avoidance of unnecessary costs of an inpatient stay for the health care system.
conditions: Traumatic lesion of the olecranon bursa

interventions.name:
Cluster A - Injury < 1cm ("small lesion") - scheme (1):
The first 20 patients in cluster A will be treated according to scheme (1).

Scheme (1) Conservative & discharge: Lavage, sterile wound dressing, immobilization, oral antibiotic therapy (outpatient).

Cluster B - Injury ≥ 1cm ("big lesion") - scheme (3):
The first 20 patients in cluster B will be treated according to scheme (3).

Scheme (3) Debridement & discharge: Surgical debridement, lavage, wound closure, immobilization, oral antibiotic therapy (outpatient).

Cluster A - Injury < 1cm ("small lesion") - scheme (2):
The following 20 patients in cluster A will be treated according to scheme (2).

Scheme (2) Bursectomy & admit: Surgical bursectomy, immobilization, intravenous antibiotic therapy (inpatient).

Cluster B - Injury ≥ 1cm ("big lesion") - scheme (2):
The following 20 patients in cluster B will be treated according to scheme (2).

Scheme (2) Bursectomy & admit: Surgical bursectomy, immobilization, intravenous antibiotic therapy (inpatient).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.) Patient at least 18 years old 
2.) Traumatic injury to the BO or BP within the last 12h.
3.) Absence of pre-existing conditions that are a contraindication to inpatient surgical procedure under general anesthesia. 
4.) Consent to study participation possible.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria: 
1.) Concomitant fracture of the affected limb.
2.) Open fractures at the affected joint.
3.) Extensive leathering/necrosis/injury/contamination of the BO or BP requiring extended surgical intervention. (BO: elbow joint; BP: knee joint). 
4.) Previous surgical intervention on the affected joint. 
5.) Dementia
6.) Alcohol abuse
7.) Patient younger than 18 years
8.) Ineligibility as judged by the study physician.
